evidence: The paper applies random forests only for multiple imputation via the missRanger package to handle 36 missing values in expired paracetamol measurements. No impurity importance scores, rankings, or p-values on variable importance are computed or reported. Main conclusions (household paracetamol prevalence 86.6%, 53% have ≥30 g, prescribed products 78.2% of total mass) derive from survey proportions and Wilson score confidence intervals, not importance-based analyses.
